name: Dutch Patriot & NASAMS Batteries — Poland
detail: Netherlands deployed two Patriot air-defence missile systems and roughly 300 personnel to Poland to protect the NATO Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine (NSATU) logistics hub near Jasionka/Rzeszów.

name: Spanish NASAMS Battery — Estonia
detail: Spain maintains a NASAMS surface-to-air missile battery deployed to Estonia under NATO's Baltic Air Policing reinforcement, with allied rotations planned to sustain coverage.

name: Italian Eurofighter Typhoon Detachment — Šiauliai AB, Lithuania
detail: Italian Air Force Eurofighter Typhoons flying NATO Baltic Air Policing missions from Šiauliai Air Base; two aircraft from this detachment took part in the August 14 Rugaji drone shootdown.

name: Turkish F-16 Detachment — Ämari AB, Estonia
detail: Turkish Air Force F-16s flying Baltic Air Policing sorties from Ämari Air Base; two aircraft supported the August 14 Rugaji intercept alongside Italian Eurofighters.

name: French Rafale Detachment — Latvia
detail: French Air Force Rafale fighters on NATO Baltic Air Policing rotation in Latvia; downed a drone near Berzgale on June 8, 2026.

name: Romanian F-16 Quick Reaction Fleet — Fetești & Câmpia Turzii
detail: Romania's F-16 fleet, operating quick-reaction alert sorties from Fetești and Câmpia Turzii airbases, has intercepted or downed multiple drones over Romanian territory and territorial waters through 2026, including the July 26 Sulina shootdown.

name: Spanish F/A-18 Detachment — Romania
detail: Spanish Air Force F/A-18 fighters deployed to Romania on a NATO air-policing rotation, coordinated through NATO's Combined Air Operations Center in Torrejón, Spain; downed a drone near Galați on August 16, 2026.

name: Polish F-16 Quick Reaction Alert Fleet
detail: Poland's national F-16 QRA fleet, scrambled repeatedly through 2026 in response to missile/drone incursions (including the July 30 Lublin incident) and to intercept Russian Il-20 reconnaissance flights over the Baltic Sea.

name: Bundeswehr Specialized Counter-Drone Unit
detail: Germany doubled its specialized counter-drone unit to roughly 300 personnel and expanded from four to eight operational bases nationwide following the August 11 Leipzig/Halle Airport explosive-drone incident.

name: NATO Integrated Air and Missile Defence (IAMD) Surge
detail: Alliance-wide reinforcement of radar, sensor, and integrated air and missile defence coverage 'from the Baltic to the Black Sea,' announced following the August 12 North Atlantic Council statement on Russian responsibility for the incursions.

name: Drone Security Technology Centre — Cochstedt, Germany
detail: New DLR-run national research centre opened August 18, 2026 at the former Cochstedt airport in Saxony-Anhalt, expanding Germany's existing National Test Centre for Unmanned Aerial Systems to research, test, and develop counter-drone detection and defence technology for airports, major events, and critical infrastructure.

name: U.S. EA-37B Compass Call — Poland/Baltic Rotation
detail: U.S. Air Force EA-37B Compass Call electronic-warfare aircraft, operating from Powidz airbase (Poland) and Souda Bay (Crete), led a 25-50 aircraft NATO air package over Poland and the Baltic near Kaliningrad on August 18, 2026, alongside a NATO E-3A Sentry AWACS, U.S./Norwegian fighters, and Polish ground forces.
